transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Dr. Miguel Alvarez (Aurora Head of Data), Sofia Patel (Aurora Legal), Jordan Kim (Aurora Platform Eng)
Meeting ID: ff-20260410-aurora-001

Summary (auto): 0:00-5:00 - Quick intro and scope. 5:00-25:00 - Console walkthrough: request storage toggles, storeless mode demo + live toggle. 25:00-40:00 - API and SDK patterns, KMS and private deployment questions. 40:00-49:00 - Recap, next steps, action items

[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can see a few faces. I'm Liam from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Dr. Miguel Alvarez: Good, thanks. Sorry, got pulled into another thread earlier but we're all set. We wanna focus mostly on how you handle PHI and whether we can avoid storing any request text
[00:15] Sofia Patel: And legal here to make sure retention windows and audit proofs align with our compliance needs, HIPAA, obviously.
[00:20] Priya Raman: Great, thanks. Quick agenda — we'll show the Console toggles for request storage, a live demo of 'storeless mode' and redaction settings, then dive into API examples and key-management. We'll also flag any perf tradeoffs.
[00:30] Jordan Kim: FYI — our infra is a mix, main EMR on-prem, but we're ok with cloud if VPC peering and no egress leaves region. Also, we have a preferred HSM for keys.
[00:38] Liam Chen: Perfect. I'll share the deck and the retention matrix link in chat. (link: retention-matrix-aurora.xlsx)

[02:10] Priya Raman: Alright, switching to the Console — bear with the slide share, network is a little slow today. So here is the tenant view and per-route controls. You can toggle 'Store Requests' per route or set a global default. When turned off— we call it 'storeless mode' — the request payload is never persisted to disk, only ephemeral memory until the response is generated.
[02:30] Miguel Alvarez: When you say 'never persisted' — does that include logs and debugging traces? We need as little footprint as possible.
[02:36] Priya Raman: Good question. By default, we still emit structured telemetry to trace requests for observability, but that's configurable. You can set telemetry to 'minimal' which only emits anonymized timing and error counters, or 'none' for the strictest posture. Also, you can enable request redaction — patterns-based PII redaction — which strips matching tokens before any persistence.
[03:05] Sofia Patel: Are the redaction rules auditable? We need to show a tamper-evident change history for legal.
[03:10] Priya Raman: Yes — changes to retention or redaction rules are stored in the Audit Log with user/time and can be exported. Those logs are SHA-256-signed in the private deployment offer, and we can integrate with your SIEM.
[03:20] Jordan Kim: Quick clarification — where do those audit logs live for hosted customers? Cloud buckets or in the console DB?
[03:24] Liam Chen: For hosted it's in our log pipeline S3-equivalent with encryption and tenant separation. For Private deployments logs stay in your VPC, same retention settings you configure.

[05:00] Speaker 2: (mumbling) I saw earlier you mentioned KMS.
[05:03] Priya Raman: Yep. We support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS and HSM integrations. In Private mode you can connect your HSM, and in Dedicated we offer a KMS passthrough. Keys can be rotated; old key material is archived per your policy. Important note — if you rotate keys frequently and keep request storage, you should plan for re-encryption windows.
[05:30] Miguel Alvarez: So for our HIPAA case, we'd prefer storeless on hosted to reduce risk. But I'm concerned about debugging if something goes wrong — we need a way to repro issues without storing PHI.
[05:44] Priya Raman: Great point. We provide a 'redacted replay' feature: you can replay the request with masked values replaced by placeholders. That keeps control-plane debug info without actual PHI. Also, for a narrow pilot you can enable ephemeral request logging that auto-deletes after a short TTL — say 1 hour — and is only available to specific roles.
[06:05] Sofia Patel: And SSO integration for RBAC? We need to restrict who can toggle these settings.
[06:08] Liam Chen: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning, fine-grained RBAC. You can scope who can change retention policies. We also support audit-only modes where changes create tickets instead of applying directly.

[08:00] Priya Raman: Moving to a live demo — I'm gonna flip the 'Store Requests' toggle off on this demo route and show a new request. Note: this is a sanitized playground, not customer data.
[08:15] [screen share noise]
[08:30] Priya Raman: Toggled off. Now I call the API — sample chat request with a mock patient name "Jane Doe" — note that our UI shows the request as 'not stored' and the trace id is ephemeral. You can see no request body in logs after the call completes.
[08:55] Jordan Kim: Can you show the network path? Is the request touching any disk, like a swap or ephemeral disk writes?
[09:05] Priya Raman: The runtime keeps content in memory and NVMe without persistent writes, and we prevent OS-level swap for those processes. For Private deployments we can mount tmpfs to guarantee RAM-only behavior. There's some nuance — very long contexts still generate KV cache entries that may spill; we have a 'no-kv-spill' mode that prioritizes latency at the cost of throughput.
[09:35] Miguel Alvarez: How does that affect latency and throughput? We can't degrade below 150ms p50 for our user-facing tools.
[09:42] Priya Raman: 'No-kv-spill' typically increases token cost because batching is reduced; latency P50 improves but throughput drops. For p50 ~150ms it's doable on Dedicated GPUs with tuned batching. We'll run a latencybench with your payloads to verify.

[11:00] Speaker 3: (brief interruption) Do you support regex-based redaction? Like SSN patterns and MRN?
[11:07] Priya Raman: Yes, rule engine supports regex, dictionary lists, and ML-based PII detectors. You can chain rules and set tiers: strict for PHI and permissive for debug. Rules are evaluated pre-persist.
[11:25] Sofia Patel: If a rule fails or mislabels, what's the rollback? We need to ensure no false positives break analytics.
[11:30] Priya Raman: Rules are versioned; you can rollback to previous rule sets and there's a dry-run mode where it annotates without removing data. We also keep a non-PII hashed fingerprint for dedupe — so analytics can run without raw values.

[13:00] Liam Chen: On the API side — if you use the Redwood SDK, there's a header you can set 'x-redwood-storeless:true' per request. That lets application developers opt into not storing just particular flows. It's helpful if you only want to disable persistence for endpoints that handle PHI.
[13:20] Jordan Kim: Can that header be enforced by policy rather than client-side? We don't trust all clients.
[13:24] Priya Raman: Yes — you can enforce route-level policies. If a route is marked 'storeless', the service ignores client headers and enforces the setting server-side. Also you can tie policies to tokens/roles so only certain tokens can override.

[15:00] Priya Raman: Let's look at the retention UI — you can set retention windows in days per tenant, per route, or per tag. Common pattern for Aurora: route A (patient-intake) = 0 days, route B (non-PHI analytics) = 90 days. You can also auto-redact after X hours using TTL rules.
[15:28] Dr. Miguel Alvarez: About TTL — do deleted records leave recoverable traces in backups or archives?
[15:32] Priya Raman: For hosted, backups are also subject to tenant retention and are purged in the same workflow. In Private deployments backups are controlled by your infra, so we'll provide scripts to rotate and securely delete per policy. We can support certified deletion flows for audit.

[17:00] Liam Chen: A quick note on encryption — data at rest is AES-256 and envelope encrypted with your KMS. In Dedicated we can offer customer-managed keys in our KMS hierarchy; in Private you use your KMS/HSM directly.
[17:18] Jordan Kim: Does key rotation require re-encrypting stored requests?
[17:22] Priya Raman: If requests are stored, yes you can choose re-encrypt or keep old keys for read-only access. Most customers with strict compliance prefer short retention so they don't need complex re-encryption.

[19:00] Speaker 2: Any limits to the 'redacted replay' feature?
[19:03] Priya Raman: Replays replace redacted tokens with placeholders; long-form hallucinations can still be present in model output but the original PII is removed. Also replays are subject to role-based access and TTL. We log replay access in the audit trail.

[21:00] Miguel Alvarez: Let's talk about private deployment cost and timelines — we may need Private in a later phase because of data residency and on-prem EMR ties. What's typical lead time?
[21:10] Liam Chen: For a Private package with our standard on-prem appliance it's typically 8-12 weeks from PO to delivery, depending on network/design approvals. Dedicated reserved capacity can be done in days if you choose the cloud-dedicated pool.
[21:30] Jordan Kim: Network setup: do you support IP allowlists, VPC peering, private endpoints?
[21:34] Priya Raman: All of the above. We recommend private endpoints and VPC peering for HIPAA customers. We'll share our network runbook and a checklist (link: redwood-network-runbook.pdf).

[24:00] Sofia Patel: A legal question — can you provide a written attestation that no data is stored if we enable storeless mode? We need to include that in the contract.
[24:07] Liam Chen: We can provide a technical attestation and a deployment checklist. For hosted customers 'storeless mode' reduces persistence risk but it's difficult to warrant 100% in hosted mode due to telemetry; however, with Private deployment you get stronger guarantees including no off-cluster persistence. We'll draft language for the pilot contract.

[26:00] Priya Raman: Going back to cost — storeless reduces storage fees but can increase per-token CPU cost due to cryptographic masking and more CPU-bound redaction. Our Optimize team recommends using model quantization and batching profiles to offset that. We can run Optimize recommendations once we have your request profile.
[26:28] Miguel Alvarez: Can Redwood's Optimize suggest exact token-cost delta for our expected load?
[26:32] Liam Chen: Yes, with sample workloads we run a cost model and show delta across policies like 'storeless', '1hr-TTL', and '90-day retention'. Priya will include a small CSV output with estimated cost per 1M requests.

[28:00] Priya Raman: Quick demo of the API logs in the Console — here's a request that had PII redacted; see the annotation that shows which rule fired. Note that the raw text column is blank because storeless was enabled.
[28:20] Jordan Kim: That's helpful. If we need to search on hashed fingerprints, do you support deterministic hashing so we can correlate events?
[28:26] Priya Raman: Yes — HMAC-based deterministic hashing with tenant-scoped salt so you can match without revealing PII.

[30:00] Speaker 4: (brief background noise) What's the expected SLAs for Private vs Dedicated?
[30:05] Liam Chen: Dedicated has SLA for throughput and latency tiers depending on commitment. Private SLAs are negotiable in enterprise contracts; typical uptime guarantees mirror Dedicated but with different support SLAs.

[32:00] Miguel Alvarez: Are there any known PCI or ISO gaps if we go for Private?
[32:05] Priya Raman: Private deployments can be set up to meet ISO 27001 and PCI if you manage the network appropriately. Our compliance package includes templates for policies and control mappings.

[34:00] Liam Chen: Ok, a quick path forward: we'll run a targeted latencybench for your sample payloads, share SOC2 + network docs, and draft pilot contract language. Any other must-haves from legal or infra now?
[34:12] Sofia Patel: Please show how change history is tamper-evident and include exportable proofs for audits.
[34:18] Priya Raman: We'll include the audit log signing details and proof-of-change export.
[34:25] Jordan Kim: From infra - we need a simple runbook for deployment and also example firewall rules.

[36:00] Priya Raman: One last note — if you need to keep some analytics running while scrubbing PHI, we recommend the 'hashed fingerprint + aggregate' pattern we discussed. That lets you do near real-time analytics without raw PII.
[36:18] Miguel Alvarez: That sounds promising.

[38:00] Speaker 2: (typo) you said KV cahce earlier — how does that interact with redaction?
[38:05] Priya Raman: Good catch — the KV cache is populated with token-level representations; when storeless is on we avoid persisting readable tokens to KV. There may be opaque cache entries; we have a 'cache-scrub' job that runs to zero them out after TTL. Sometimes the transcriber writes 'kay-vee' — that's normal in the notes.

[40:00] Liam Chen: Alright we're coming up on time. Recap of next steps in chat: I'll attach SOC2, retention matrix, network runbook; Priya will run bench and share results; Aurora to confirm PHI categories and peering windows.
[40:22] Priya Raman: Also adding the pilot scope doc and a sample policy snippet for enforcement.

[42:00] Sofia Patel: A final legal ask — include indemnity language limited to gross negligence; otherwise we can't sign. We'll review the pilot addendum.
[42:08] Liam Chen: Noted, will loop in Legal.

[44:00] Miguel Alvarez: Thanks everyone. Let's plan a 60-minute pilot kickoff in two weeks if docs look good.
[44:06] Liam Chen: Sounds great. We'll propose times.
[44:12] Jordan Kim: Thanks, appreciate the detail.

[46:00] Speaker 1: (closing) meeting end
